deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics and is not by Riemann. It is the last page (closing and signature) of a letter by Erwin Papperitz (1857–1938), filed in the Riemann Nachlass bundle 'R.PFunctionen'. The previous page shows the letter's context. Papperitz is answering an editor or scholar ('verehrter Herr Professor') who asked which literature bears on Riemann's theory of P-functions and hypergeometric functions. The topics are the normalization of the branches of hypergeometric functions and integral representations. Earlier in the letter he discusses Thomae's normalization (the first coefficient in the expansion of each branch is set to 1). He discusses Pochhammer's 'Doppelumlauf': the double-loop contour around two singular points a and b, traversed in the positive and negative senses. With it Pochhammer obtains the six fundamental integrals of the hypergeometric equation (formulas (53), (54) of his paper). He also discusses Klein's normalization in homogeneous variables, which Papperitz regards as distinguished, while Thomae's appears arbitrary. On this page he concludes as follows. He hopes he has met the correspondent's wish as far as possible. He knows of no further works important for the question. The connected exposition of the theory 'from the pen of one of his students', announced by Klein ('a. a. O. p. 151'), has to his knowledge not yet appeared. Then come the formal closing and the signature 'Ihr ergebenster Erwin Papperitz'. There is no derivation to reconstruct. Historical context (my inference): the letter dates from the 1890s or around 1900. Papperitz is known for the 1889 paper in which the Riemann–Papperitz equation appears explicitly. The recipient was plausibly someone preparing Riemann's posthumous material, e.g. for the Nachträge (1902) to Riemann's Werke. The recipient's identity, the exact Klein reference, and the date are unsure.
